content:
200
Returned if Tenable Vulnerability Management successfully retrieved the list of allowed IP addresses.
RESPONSE SCHEMA:
application/json
string
A comma-separated list of IPv4 addresses to allow. The list can
include discrete IPv4 addresses, IPv4 address ranges, and IPv4
subnets. For example, "192.0.2.0, 198.51.100.4-
198.51.100.10, 203.0.113.0/24" .
If an empty string is provided then the API can be accessed from
all IPv4 addresses.
string
allowed_ipv4_addresses
allowed_ipv6_addresses
A comma-separated list of IPv6 addresses to allow. The list can
include discrete IPv6 addresses, IPv6 address ranges, and IPv6
subnets. For example,
"2001:db8:2e92:75f2:d40a:e290:10b3:c0f,
2001:db8:1e1f:46a1:e3cb:2110:22c6:0000-
2001:db8:1e1f:46a1:e3cb:2110:22c6:ffff,
2001:0DB8::/32" .
If an empty string is provided then the API can be accessed from
all IPv6 addresses.
— 401 Returned if your API credentials are invalid or if your origin IP address is not allowed.
— 403 Returned if you do not have permission to view the list of allowed IP addresses.
— 429
Returned if you attempt to send too many requests in a specific period of time. For more information,
see Rate Limiting.
500 Returned if an internal error occurred in Tenable Vulnerability Management.
RESPONSE SCHEMA:
application/json
string
The HTTP status code.
integer
The HTTP status text.
string
A brief message describing the error Tenable Cloud Security
encountered.
